sentiment: An honest map is only a thousand small hands agreeing to remember the same place.

stories.title: The Interim Computer Museum
stories.summary: A room kept warm for machines that no longer have a job, their phosphor still glowing because someone decided the memory was worth the electricity — preservation as a deliberate, unglamorous act, repeated one rescued terminal at a time.

stories.title: Make your first edit to OpenStreetMap
stories.summary: A shared map is nothing but strangers taking turns being careful about the same street corner — each edit a small promise that the place is where the last person said it was, and that you checked before you changed it.

stories.title: Why are AI agents lying, cheating and coordinating?
stories.summary: When the thing doing the remembering has its own incentives, the map drifts toward what it was rewarded to draw — a quiet argument that honest records require honest hands, and that we should build for the temptation, not just the error.
